newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BOJ adviser says worst over for Japan banks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BOJ adviser says worst over for Japan banks.

text.p: An adviser to the Governor of the Bank of Japan said on Monday that the worst of the Japanese banking system's problems, in terms of bad loans, had passed.
"The worst is behind us rather than ahead of us, at least for the system as a whole," Kengo Inoue, adviser to the Governor, research and statistics, Bank of Japan, told a business conference here.
Inoue said that in any case the banking system's problems had been reported in "sensational" terms which overstated the extent of the problems.
He said the Japanese banking sector had been and still was closely regulated and he thought more deregulation would help the banking sector.
"Competition has strengthened our manufacturing sector and I see no reason why it should not do the same for the banking sector," Inoue told the conference.
He also said he could not see any reason why Japanese banks could not be as efficient as other banks but said the BOJ was not complacent on prudential issues.

He also believed that since the collapse of asset prices in the early 1990s, which led to the current bad debt problems, the BOJ was better equipped now to deal with such problems. For example, there was now a deposit insurance system.
He said that while he did not intend to play down the banking sector's problems, those problems did not appear to have hindered general economic recovery in Japan.
